subject.title: ClawSweeper can leave stale review-started placeholders and repeatedly re-trigger the same issue

question: Should an expired or blocked ClawSweeper review retain one editable status comment with a terminal/backoff state, rather than creating a new visible review-started placeholder for each retry?
rationale: The report establishes notification noise and ambiguity, but the intended retention, retry budget, and maintainer-decision suppression policy is not established by current-source evidence.

options.title: Adopt durable status lifecycle
options.body: Use one marker-backed status comment per item, edit it to completed, failed, stale, or awaiting maintainer decision, and back off duplicate retries.

options.title: Keep per-attempt comments
options.body: Retain separate start comments but add explicit terminal comments and a bounded retry budget, accepting higher notification volume.

recommendation.title: Adopt durable status lifecycle
recommendation.body: Use one marker-backed status comment per item, edit it to completed, failed, stale, or awaiting maintainer decision, and back off duplicate retries.

likelyOwner.reason: The bot is the only concrete actor identified in the supplied review-status timeline; human code ownership requires a successful history inspection.
